extracted.intended_audience: Hacker News users — people who read, submit, comment, flag, or moderate on news.ycombinator.com
extracted.subtask_description: Site-specific FAQ and rules for submitting stories/polls/questions, commenting, flagging, voting, and other community-moderation behaviors on Hacker News. Covers ranking, karma, content policies, and account/profile actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and comment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there rules about submissions and comments? (link to https://news.ycombinator.com/newsguidelines.html)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the linked newsguidelines for the site's detailed rules on what belongs on HN.

rubrics_metrics.name: How stories and comments are ranked
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic algorithm divides points by a power of the time since a story was submitted. Comments in threads are ranked the same way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other factors affecting rank include user flags, anti-abuse software, software which demotes overheated discussions, account or site weighting, and moderator action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Karma calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Roughly, the number of upvotes on their posts minus the number of downvotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These don't match up exactly. Some votes are dropped by anti-abuse software.

rubrics_metrics.name: User karma does not boost post ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Do posts by users with more karma rank higher? No.

rubrics_metrics.name: Down arrows availability
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no down arrows on stories. They appear on comments after users reach a certain karma threshold, but never on direct replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: What kind of formatting can you use in comments? (link to http://news.ycombinator.com/formatdoc)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the formatdoc for supported markup/formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit a question (Ask HN)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the submit link in the top bar, and leave the url field blank.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit a poll
rubrics_metrics.description: How do I submit a poll? (link to http://news.ycombinator.com/newpoll)

rubrics_metrics.name: Links in text submissions are not allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: How do I make a link in a text submission? You can't.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is to prevent people from submitting a link with their comments in a privileged position at the top of the page. If you want to submit a link with comments, submit the link, then add a regular comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask HN vs Show HN definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask HN lists questions and other text submissions. Show HN is for sharing your personal work and has special rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask/Show visibility thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Why hasn't my submission appeared on Ask HN or Show HN? All Ask HNs appear on newest and asknew, and all Show HNs on newest and shownew, but there is a small points threshold before a post makes it to ask or show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Green usernames indicate new accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: What do green usernames mean? Green indicates a new account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faded comments indicate downvotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Why are some comments faded? Faded text means that a comment has been downvoted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can read the comment in normal text by clicking on its timestamp to go to its page.

rubrics_metrics.name: [flagged] status meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: What does [flagged] mean? Users flagged the post as breaking the guidelines or otherwise not belonging on HN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators sometimes also add [flagged] (though not usually on submissions), and sometimes turn flags off when they are unfair.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to flag a comment
rubrics_metrics.description: How do I flag a comment? Click on its timestamp to go to its page, then click the 'flag' link at the top.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There's a small karma threshold before flag links appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: [dead] status meaning and vouching
rubrics_metrics.description: What does [dead] mean? The post was killed by software, user flags, or moderators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dead posts aren't displayed by default, but you can see them all by turning on 'showdead' in your profile. If you see a [dead] post that shouldn't be dead, you can vouch for it: click on its timestamp to go to its page, then click 'vouch' at the top. When enough users do this, the post is restored. There's a small karma threshold before vouch links appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: [deleted] status meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: What does [deleted] mean? The author deleted the post, or asked us to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike dead posts, these remain deleted even when showdead is turned on.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'hide' link behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: What do 'hide' links do? They remove a submission from your personal view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Others still see it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repost policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Are reposts ok? If a story has not had significant attention in the last year or so, a small number of reposts is ok.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Otherwise we bury reposts as duplicates. Please don't delete and repost the same story. Deletion is for things that shouldn't have been submitted in the first place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paywall policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Are paywalls ok? It's ok to post stories from sites with paywalls that have workarounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In comments, it's ok to ask how to read an article and to help other users do so. But please don't post complaints about paywalls. Those are off topic. More here (link).

rubrics_metrics.name: No solicitation for upvotes or comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Can I ask people to upvote my submission? No.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should vote for a story because they personally find it intellectually interesting, not because someone has content to promote. We penalize or ban submissions, accounts, and sites that break this rule. Can I ask people to comment on my submission? No, for the same reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Job ads policy and designated threads
rubrics_metrics.description: Can I post a job ad? Please don't post job ads as submissions to HN. A regular 'Who Is Hiring?' thread appears on the first weekday of each month (or Jan 2). Most job ads are welcome there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only an account called whoishiring is allowed to submit the thread itself. This prevents a race to post it first. Another kind of job ad is reserved for YC-funded startups. These appear on the front page, but are not stories: they have no vote arrows, points, or comments. They begin part-way down and fall steadily. Only one is on the front page at a time. The rest are listed at jobs.

rubrics_metrics.name: YC ownership and editorial independence
rubrics_metrics.description: What's the relationship between YC and HN? Y Combinator owns and funds HN. The HN team is editorially independent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HN gives three features to YC: job ads and startup launches get placed on the front page, and YC founder names are displayed to other YC alumni in orange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of negative stories about YC
rubrics_metrics.description: Are negative stories about YC suppressed on HN? No, we moderate less, not more, when YC or a YC startup is the topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The good will of the community is worth more than any story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thread closing conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Why can't I post a comment to a thread? Threads are closed to new comments after two weeks, or if the submission has been killed by software, moderators, or user flags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank cannot be derived solely from votes and time
rubrics_metrics.description: Why is A ranked below B even though A has more points and is newer? You can't derive rank from votes and time alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'How are stories ranked?' — other factors influence rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profile 'delay' setting
rubrics_metrics.description: In my profile, what is delay? It gives you time to edit your comments before they appear to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set it to the number of minutes you'd like. The maximum is 10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profile 'noprocrast' setting
rubrics_metrics.description: In my profile, what is noprocrast? It's a way to help you prevent yourself from spending too much time on HN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you turn it on you'll only be allowed to visit the site for maxvisit minutes at a time, with gaps of minaway minutes in between. The defaults are 20 and 180 (20 minutes on, then 3 hours off).

rubrics_metrics.name: Password reset procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: How do I reset my password? If you have an email address in your profile, you can do that here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you haven't, email hn@ycombinator.com for help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing username
rubrics_metrics.description: Can I change my username? Yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email hn@ycombinator.com and we'll help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account deletion and privacy requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Can I delete my account? We try not to delete entire account histories because that would gut the threads the account had participated in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, we care about protecting individual users and take care of privacy requests every day, so if we can help, please email hn@ycombinator.com. We don't want anyone to get in trouble from anything they posted to HN. More here (link).

rubrics_metrics.name: IP bans and unbanning
rubrics_metrics.description: My IP address seems to be banned. How can I unban it? If you request many pages quickly, your IP address might get banned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This self-serve unbanning procedure works most of the time. If not, email hn@ycombinator.com.
